modules.name: exposure
modules.purpose: Brightens or darkens the whole photo, like changing exposure in camera.

custom_widgets.what: area picker on the exposure slider sets exposure from the selected area
area exposure mapping: pick a control sample, shows input/target color swatches (drawing areas) and maps it to the target lightness

image_actions: area picker on exposure slider (set exposure from selected area)
area exposure mapping (match control sample to target lightness)
automatic deflicker from raw histogram (mode = automatic)
modules.notes: Mode combobox is insensitive and forced to manual for non-raw/non-mosaiced images (exposure.c:670-675). The two toggle labels are rewritten at runtime with the camera values: 'compensate camera exposure (%+.1f EV)' and 'highlight preservation mode (%.1f EV)' (exposure.c:687,697); the hilite toggle is only visible when the camera reports a highlight bias > 0 (exposure.c:705). 'area exposure mapping' collapsible section is GUI-only state (darkroom conf), not params. Multi-instance useful for masked exposure. Control notes — mode: 'automatic' = deflicker; only available on raw images; area mode: GUI-only (not a param); values correction/measure; lightness: GUI-only target lightness stored in darkroom/modules/exposure/lightness; created with digits 1 (exposure.c:1314).

modules.name: filmic rgb
modules.purpose: Compresses the scene's dynamic range into the display with a filmic S-curve and protects highlights.

controls.label: structure ↔ texture
controls.visible_when: sensitive only if reconstruction enabled and bloom ↔ reconstruct != -100

controls.label: bloom ↔ reconstruct
controls.visible_when: sensitive only if highlight reconstruction enabled

controls.label: gray ↔ colorful details
controls.visible_when: sensitive only if highlight reconstruction enabled

custom_widgets.what: shows the filmic curve / dynamic range zones; click to switch views
area pickers on the scene sliders and 'auto tune levels'

modules.notes: Interactive graph above the notebook (action 'graph', filmicrgb.c:4352) plus notebook action 'page'. Defaults depend on the image: for raw files in scene-referred workflow black/white relative exposure are shifted by the camera exposure bias (filmicrgb.c:3163-3175) and output_power recomputed. With the default color science v7 (2023) the 'saturation' slider is labelled 'highlights saturation mix' and 'preserve chrominance' is hidden (filmicrgb.c:4677-4705); v3/v6 call it 'extreme luminance saturation', v4/v5 'mid-tones saturation'. 'RGB euclidean norm (legacy)' is removed from the preserve chrominance list (filmicrgb.c:4575-4576). middle gray luminance / target middle gray only visible with 'use custom middle-gray values' (filmicrgb.c:4746). hardness hidden when auto adjust hardness is on (default). Moving threshold/transition auto-enables highlight reconstruction. Params spline_version and compensate_icc_black have no GUI. Percent sliders here already store percent (hard max > 10), factor 1. Control notes — graph: interactive curve/zone view; clicks toggle view modes; white relative exposure: default shifted per image (see notes); black relative exposure: default shifted per image (see notes); auto tune levels: area picker setting grey/white/black from the image; display highlight reconstruction mask: GUI-only mask preview; highlights saturation mix: label depends on color science: v7 'highlights saturation mix' (default), v3/v6 'extreme luminance saturation' (introspection description), v4/v5 'mid-tones saturation'. dt_bauhaus_widget_set_label defines a new action per label (bauhaus.c:1066), so 'extreme luminance saturation' (from gui_init) and the version-specific label both exist as action paths.

modules.name: filmic
modules.purpose: Old (2018) filmic tone mapper: log shaper plus S-curve; replaced by filmic rgb.

custom_widgets.what: read-only preview of the filmic curve
area pickers on the log shaper sliders and auto tune levels

modules.notes: Deprecated (filmic.c:167): 'better use filmic rgb module instead' (filmic.c:174). No introspection ranges: every slider is built by hand with dt_bauhaus_slider_new_with_range and callbacks; defaults from init (filmic.c:1298-1313). 'extreme luminance saturation' is non-linear: shown s = (10^(p/100)-1)/9*100, stored p = log10(9*s/100+1)*100 (filmic.c:867, 1567). 'intent' combobox maps contrasted/faded/linear/optimized to interpolator 0/1/2/3. preserve the chrominance is a plain GtkCheckButton. 'destination/display' is a collapsible expander. Control notes — graph: read-only curve preview; extreme luminance saturation: non-linear: displayed s = (10^(p/100)-1)/9*100; default p=100 -> s=100; preserve the chrominance: GtkCheckButton, no bauhaus action.

modules.name: sigmoid
modules.purpose: Maps the bright scene into a pleasing display image with a smooth S-curve (contrast + skew).
modules.notes: Default scene-referred tone mapper candidate together with filmic rgb / AgX; a typical edit needs only contrast. Two collapsible sections: 'primaries' (only visible when color processing == per channel, sigmoid.c:873) and 'display luminance'. base primaries is created on self, so its action has no 'primaries/' prefix (sigmoid.c:920), while the inset/rotation/purity sliders use section 'primaries'. Target black/white params are already in percent (hard max > 10, so no x100 factor): 0.0152 is shown as 0.0152%. Rotation displayed in degrees via factor 180/pi.

custom_widgets.what: read-only plot of the tone curve (collapsible 'show curve')
area pickers on exposure range and pivot sliders, plus 'auto tune levels'

modules.notes: Notebook action 'page' (agx.c:2455). An optional 'curve' tab between settings and primaries only exists when conf plugins/darkroom/agx/enable_curve_tab is set (agx.c:2468); then the basic curve box is reparented between tabs. 'look' is a collapsible section unless conf look_always_visible. In scene-referred workflow reload_defaults replaces the introspection defaults with Blender-like primaries (agx.c:2707-2711, values at agx.c:317-345), e.g. base primaries Rec2020, red attenuation 0.2946, master rotation reversal 0. 'pivot relative exposure' is shown in EV with a DYNAMIC factor/offset: factor = white EV - black EV, offset = black EV (agx.c:1011-1012); with defaults factor 16.5, offset -10, so param 0.6061 shows 0 EV. Purity/hue slider reset defaults are forced to 0, master ratios to 1 (agx.c:2203,2228,2365,2373). Many advanced params; for Omalux probably expose exposure range + contrast + look. Control notes — auto tune levels: area picker sets black/white relative exposure; read exposure: camera icon button; reads exposure params (from the exposure module); pivot relative exposure: factor/offset are dynamic: factor = white - black relative exposure, offset = black relative exposure (agx.c:1004-1019); values here are for the defaults; graph: read-only curve plot in collapsible 'show curve'; reset primaries: menu: blender-like / smooth / unmodified primaries.

modules.name: base curve
modules.purpose: Applies a camera-maker style tone curve to make raw files look like the camera JPEG.

custom_widgets.what: drag/add/remove nodes of the RGB tone curve

image_actions: per-camera base curve preset applied automatically on load
modules.notes: Default params may be replaced by a per-camera base curve preset when the image loads (basecurve.c:495-520, conf plugins/darkroom/basecurve/auto_apply_percamera_presets); not enabled by default. Only curve [0] is edited in the GUI (minmax_curve from basecurve[0], basecurve.c:2082-2086); basecurve[3][20] nodes, MAXNODES 20. 'fusion' is an int param shown as combobox with manually added entries (basecurve.c:2101-2104). exposure bias: param default 1.0 but the slider's reset default is overridden to 0 (basecurve.c:2117). 'scale for graph' is GUI-only. Control notes — curve: draggable spline nodes (input x, output y, 0..1), log-scale view via 'scale for graph'; exposure bias: slider reset default is 0 (basecurve.c:2117), param default 1.0; scale for graph: GUI-only log scale of the graph.

modules.notes: Curve editor with L/a/b channel tabs (action 'channel'); tabs only shown when color space == 'Lab, independent channels' (tonecurve.c:979). tonecurve[3][20] nodes; default L curve (0,0)-(1,1), a/b 3 nodes through 0.5 (tonecurve.c:924-932). The interpolation combobox writes tonecurve_type for all three channels (tonecurve.c:993-1002). tonecurve_preset and tonecurve_unbound_ab have no GUI. Enum order in the color space combobox follows declaration order (1,0,2,3). 'scale for graph' is GUI-only. Control notes — curve: per-channel node curve, channel chosen by L/a/b tabs; pick color: shows picked input/output values on the curve; scale for graph: GUI-only.

custom_widgets.what: drag/add/remove nodes per channel over a histogram
show picked color on curve / create curve from picked area

R/G/B tabs (action 'channel') only shown in 'RGB, independent channels'; preserve colors only in linked mode (rgblevels.c:215-231). No sliders at all; a slider mapping would be three sliders per channel. Control notes — auto region: draw a region for auto levels.

modules.name: levels
modules.purpose: Sets black, middle gray and white points on a histogram (Lab lightness).

custom_widgets.what: drag black/gray/white handles over the L histogram
three point pickers for black, medium gray and white point

modules.notes: Deprecated (levels.c:122): 'please use the RGB levels module instead' (levels.c:109). Manual mode is a histogram with three draggable handles writing levels[3] (default 0, 0.5, 1; levels.c:589-591); automatic mode uses three percentile sliders. Control notes — levels: levels[0..2] = black/gray/white input points in 0..1 via draggable handles; auto: apply auto levels; black: black percentile; gray: gray percentile; white: white percentile.

modules.name: tone equalizer
modules.purpose: Brightens or darkens specific brightness zones (shadows, mid-tones, highlights) while keeping local contrast.

custom_widgets.what: drag the exposure-per-zone curve over the luminance histogram
hover image to read zone exposure, scroll to brighten/darken the zone under the cursor

image_actions: on-canvas scroll edits the zone under the cursor
modules.notes: Notebook action 'page' (toneequal.c:3233). The nine 'simple' sliders are first labelled by their introspection descriptions (blacks, deep shadows, shadows, light shadows, mid-tones, dark highlights, highlights, whites, speculars) and then relabelled to '-8 EV' .. '+0 EV' in section 'simple' (toneequal.c:3266-3274), so their action paths are 'simple/-8 EV' etc.; the description-based actions ('blacks', 'deep shadows', ...) are also registered because each dt_bauhaus_widget_set_label call defines an action (bauhaus.c:1066). 'edges refinement/feathering' contains a slash in its label, which darktable's action path may interpret as a section separator (unclear). The 'advanced' tab is a drawn graph editing the same nine values plus 'curve smoothing', a GUI slider (-2.33..+1.67) that writes smoothing = sqrt(2)^(1+value) (toneequal.c:1765) — non-linear. On-canvas: hover shows the exposure under the cursor; scrolling over the image raises/lowers that zone (scrolled(), toneequal.c:2172). Quad 'wand' buttons on mask exposure/contrast compensation auto-adjust them from the image. Masking-tab visibility depends on 'preserve details' (toneequal.c:1665-1697). Multi-instance with masks is common. For Omalux the nine EV sliders map directly; masking stays advanced. Control notes — -8 EV: introspection description 'blacks'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3266; -7 EV: introspection description 'deep shadows'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3267; -6 EV: introspection description 'shadows'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3268; -5 EV: introspection description 'light shadows'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3269; -4 EV: introspection description 'mid-tones'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3270; -3 EV: introspection description 'dark highlights'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3271; -2 EV: introspection description 'highlights'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3272; -1 EV: introspection description 'whites'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3273; +0 EV: introspection description 'speculars'; relabelled at toneequal.c:3274; graph: drag the 9-band exposure curve; same params as the simple sliders; curve smoothing: GUI value v, param smoothing = sqrt(2)^(1+v); param default sqrt(2) -> v = 0; display exposure mask: GUI-only mask preview.

Entire UI is a drawn zone bar plus preview; size 4..24 via mouse wheel (zonesystem.c:635), zone[] = -1 means unset marker. No bauhaus sliders. modules.name: graduated density

custom_widgets.what: drag the gradient line on the image to move/rotate it
point picker on hue sets filter hue/saturation from the image

modules.notes: 'offset' (and rotation) are set by dragging the line on canvas; offset has no introspection range and no slider. Rotation is displayed with factor -1. Hue displayed 0..360 deg via factor 360. Multi-instance useful (e.g. sky + foreground). Control notes — offset: position of the gradient line, only via on-canvas drag.

modules.name: highlight reconstruction
modules.purpose: Recovers detail and color in blown-out highlights of raw photos.

controls.label: noise level
controls.visible_when: (method == guided laplacians && bayer) || (method == segmentation based && rebuild != off)

image_actions: visualize clipped highlights / segments (mask display toggles on sliders)
modules.notes: Single instance, raw-only in practice (enabled by default for raw; non-raw forced to 'clip highlights', highlights.c:1144). The method list is rebuilt per sensor type in reload_defaults (highlights.c:1222-1250): non-raw -> clip only; sraw -> opposed + clip; bayer -> all up to guided laplacians; xtrans -> up to segmentation based (no guided laplacians). Monochrome shows 'not applicable'. Quad buttons on clip/combine/candidating/strength toggle false-color mask visualisation (GUI-only). blendL/blendC are unused. Control notes — method: value list depends on sensor (see notes); combobox order follows enum declaration.

modules.name: contrast brightness saturation
modules.purpose: Simple contrast, brightness and saturation sliders.
modules.notes: Deprecated (IOP_FLAGS_DEPRECATED, colisa.c:93): 'please use colorbalance RGB module instead' (colisa.c:76). Hidden from the module list for new edits but kept for old histories/styles; Omalux already registers all three.

modules.name: local contrast
modules.purpose: Boosts or softens fine detail and texture (clarity).
modules.notes: Two sliders share one param each: sigma_s = 'coarseness' (bilateral) or 'shadows' (local laplacian); sigma_r = 'contrast' (bilateral) or 'highlights' (local laplacian) (bilat.c:447-450). Switching mode copies the visible slider values into the params (bilat.c:378-390). GUI defaults for coarseness/contrast are overridden to 50/20 via dt_bauhaus_slider_set_default (bilat.c:454,462) while the param default is 0.5. 'detail' has offset 100 + percent factor 100: raw 0.25 is shown as 125% — Omalux registry currently shows 25% for the same raw value, which deviates from darktable's display. Multi-instance useful with masks.

modules.name: fill light
modules.purpose: Lifts or lowers a chosen brightness range with a soft fill light.

custom_widgets.what: drag the center lightness of the fill light on a black-to-grey gradient
pick median lightness of an area to set center

modules.notes: Deprecated (relight.c:88): 'please use the tone equalizer module instead' (relight.c:93). 'center' is a custom gradient slider (no introspection range, 0..1 lightness) with a median-lightness picker. Control notes — center: dtgtk gradient slider over lightness 0..1; ctrl+click selects an area.

modules.name: lowlight vision
modules.purpose: Simulates how the eye sees at night: darker areas lose color and turn bluish.

custom_widgets.what: drag nodes to set how much night vision applies per brightness

modules.notes: Main control is a 6-node curve (transition_x/transition_y, DT_IOP_LOWLIGHT_BANDS=6) drawn on a graph from 'dark' to 'bright' (x) and 'day vision' to 'night vision' (y) (lowlight.c:630-652); default x = k/5 (lowlight.c:288), y = 0.5. Presets (daylight, indoor bright, ... ) carry most of the usefulness. Needs a curve widget; not a slider mapping. Control notes — graph: 6 draggable nodes; mouse-wheel changes node height.

modules.name: unbreak input profile
modules.purpose: Fixes flat or log-encoded images by undoing a gamma or applying a log curve.

custom_widgets.what: area pickers on each log slider plus 'auto tune levels'

modules.notes: Single instance (profile_gamma.c:110). Mode stack: gamma page (linear, gamma) or log page (middle gray luma, black relative exposure, dynamic range, safety factor, auto tune levels). Default mode is logarithmic. Control notes — auto tune levels: area picker that sets grey point, black exposure and dynamic range.

modules.name: negadoctor
modules.purpose: Turns scanned color or black-and-white film negatives into positives with film/paper controls.

custom_widgets.what: pick the film base / shadow cast / illuminant color in a color dialog
area pickers measure film base, shadows, illuminant, D max, scan bias, paper black and print exposure from the image

modules.notes: Single instance (negadoctor.c:150). Notebook tabs registered as action 'page' (negadoctor.c:837). Array sliders Dmin[i], wb_low[i], wb_high[i] get explicit labels; with film stock 'black and white film' the G/B Dmin sliders are hidden and Dmin[0] is relabelled 'D min' (negadoctor.c:468-472). 'print exposure adjustment' is NON-LINEAR: the slider shows log2(param) in EV over -1..+1 and writes param = 2^EV (negadoctor.c:1039,1063); default shown = log2(0.9245) = -0.113 EV, introspection range 0.5..2. D_max and scan exposure bias are shown with ' dB' suffix (density). Default Dmin = {1.00, 0.45, 0.25} set in init (negadoctor.c:386-388). Color buttons and samplers per section ('pickers/film material', 'pickers/shadows', 'pickers/illuminant'). Control notes — color of the film base: GtkColorButton editing Dmin[0..2]; film material: area picker for the film base color; D min red component: labelled 'D min' when film stock is black and white; shadows color swatch: GtkColorButton editing wb_low[0..2]; illuminant color swatch: GtkColorButton editing wb_high[0..2]; print exposure adjustment: GUI value is log2(param) EV; param = 2^value. Introspection range 0.5..2 (linear), param default 0.9245.

modules.name: invert
modules.purpose: Turns a scanned film negative into a positive using the film base color.

controls.label: color of film material
controls.action: pick color of film material from image

custom_widgets.what: pick the film base (unexposed border) color from an area
choose film material color in a color dialog

image_actions: picker: film material color from area
modules.notes: Deprecated (invert.c:143): 'please use the negadoctor module instead' (invert.c:125). Single instance. Works on raw data (filters). Only control is the film base color (color button + area picker); the label reads 'brightness of film material' on monochrome images (invert.c:410). Control notes — color of film material: GtkColorButton; action registered as 'pick color of film material from image' (invert.c:493).
